script: Spread and total were not saved for LA at Denver, so this script is inferred only from weeks 1-2 form. LA has split the run — Kyren Williams 23 carries for 126 yards, Blake Corum 22 for 133 — and poured the pass game through Davante Adams (16 targets, 221 yards, 271 air yards), while Denver has given JK Dobbins 18 carries for 72 yards and Jaylen Waddle the downfield work at 13 targets, 140 yards and 166 air yards. Bo Nix at -0.55 EPA per dropback versus the blitz on 23 dropbacks, into an LA defense that blitzes 30% and has allowed 2 passes of 20-plus on 68 attempts, points to a Denver offense that shortens rather than explodes.
who_goes_off: Davante Adams is the Rams pass-catcher set to go off: 221 yards on 16 targets and 271 air yards in weeks 1-2, into a Denver defense allowing 9.36 yards per attempt on 22 throws to the left and 5 passes of 20-plus on 60 attempts. Blake Corum is the run piece, 133 yards on 22 carries (6.05 per carry) against a Denver front allowing 5.41 yards per carry and 7 runs of 10-plus, with Kyren Williams alongside at 126 rush yards on 23 carries plus 36 receiving yards on 5 targets.
weak_spot: Denver's real leak is the left side at 9.36 yards per attempt on 22 attempts, versus 3.86 on the right (22 attempts) and 6.83 in the middle (12 attempts), plus a run defense at 5.41 yards per carry with 7 gains of 10-plus. LA's only soft patch is the middle at 6.29 yards per attempt on 14 throws; the left is 5.1 on 30 attempts and the right is 4.32 on 22, and LA has allowed just 2 passes of 20-plus on 68 attempts.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for LA at Denver, so there is no fallout to price and the weeks 1-2 usage is the role: Adams 16 targets, Terrance Ferguson 10, Puka Nacua 9 and Kyren Williams 5 for the Rams, and Jaylen Waddle 13, Courtland Sutton 9, Pat Bryant 7 and Evan Engram 6 for Denver.
qb_vs_blitz: Matthew Stafford is -0.16 EPA per dropback versus the blitz on 15 dropbacks and +0.22 when Denver does not blitz, so Denver's 34% blitz rate trims him without wiping out Adams' 271 air yards. Bo Nix is the mismatch: -0.55 EPA on 23 blitzed dropbacks versus +0.16 unblitzed, and LA blitzes 30%, which is why Sutton's 36 yards on 71 air yards are more likely to stay stuck than to catch Waddle's 140.

picks.why: Adams is at 221 receiving yards on 16 targets and 271 air yards in weeks 1-2, a 110.5-yard per-game pace against a 71.5 line, and Denver has allowed 9.36 yards per attempt to the left on 22 throws plus 5 passes of 20-plus on 60 attempts — the same shot profile as those 271 air yards.

Sutton has 36 receiving yards on 9 targets and 71 air yards in weeks 1-2, an 18-yard per-game pace against a 36.5 line, and he is running into LA's perimeter (5.1 YPA left on 30 attempts, 4.32 right on 22) plus a defense that has allowed 2 passes of 20-plus on 68 attempts while Nix is at -0.55 EPA on 23 blitzed dropbacks against a 30% LA blitz.
